land.text: the north of the Haitian state of Dessalines, taken by Christophe after the assassination of 17 October 1806

predecessors.note: The pages opened name the north only as "the north" and "the Plaine-du-Nord"; the four departments are the researcher's reading, shared with the haiti dossier's split event.

land.text: the northern kingdom, reunited with the south by President Boyer after Christophe's death on 8 October 1820

successors.note: "Boyer reunited the two parts of Haiti" (Henri Christophe page); the Kingdom page says "later that year".

capitals.name: Milot
capitals.note: State of Haiti infobox: "Capital: Milot". Coordinates approximate; Milot is not in the gazetteer (about 12 km south of Cap-Haïtien).

capitals.name: Cap-Henri (Cap-Haïtien)
capitals.note: Kingdom infobox: "Capital: Cap-Henri". Sans-Souci was the "principal royal residence", "largely completed by 1813".

rulers.name: Henri Christophe (President, then King Henri I)
rulers.note: Provisional Chief from 17 October 1806; president of the State of Haiti from 17 February 1807 (life post); king from 28 March 1811; died by his own hand on 8 October 1820.

rulers.name: Jacques-Victor (son and heir)
rulers.note: "His son and heir, Jacques-Victor, was assassinated 10 days later" (Henri Christophe page); the Kingdom page says the insurgents hanged "the new king" on 18 October 1820.

correction.text: 'Christophe created the authoritarian State of Haiti in the north' (History of Haiti); his kingdom was 'in the North'; Pétion held the south

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no row (its Haiti rows are 1792-1802 and the Empire of Haiti from 1805). None of the five pages opened gives the northern state's departments, its area or the line with Pétion's republic; the Kingdom page says only that after several battles Christophe 'managed ... to secure the borders of his new state'. The four departments (Nord, Nord-Est, Nord-Ouest, Artibonite) are the researcher's reading, matching the haiti dossier's split event. The infobox comparison could not be made (no area on either page).

region.text: the north: Christophe 'retreated with his followers to the Plaine-du-Nord'

ledger.note: 17 October 1806: Christophe founds the State of Haiti in the north. 'It was created on 17 October 1806 following the assassination of Emperor Jacques I.' The page names the north, not departments.

region.text: the border country between Christophe's north and Pétion's south (the page names no place)

ledger.note: 1807: the war with Pétion's south begins. The Kingdom page says the wars with the south 'continued intermittently from 1807 until Pétion's death in 1818'. Page silent on where the fighting was: the Artibonite is the researcher's bridging reading.

region.text: the border country between north and south

ledger.note: 1810: a peace treaty splits the country in two. The Pétion page says the struggle 'dragged on until 1810, a peace treaty was agreed to, and the country was split in two'; the Kingdom page has intermittent war to 1818, so the line stays soft.

28 March 1811: Christophe is proclaimed King Henri I. 'On 28 March 1811 President Henri was proclaimed King Henri I, thereby dissolving the State of Haiti.' Coronation 2 June 1811. The same state, the same land: a rename.

region.text: the northern kingdom, reunited by Boyer after Christophe's death

ledger.note: October 1820: Christophe takes his own life and Boyer reunites Haiti. 'he promptly shot himself on 8 October 1820' (Kingdom page); 'Boyer came to power and reunited the two parts of Haiti' (Henri Christophe page). The Kingdom page puts the union 'later that year'.

region.text: the Kingdom of Haiti, ended by Christophe's death and the revolt of the northern provinces

ledger.note: 1820: the Kingdom of Haiti ends. 'By 1820, opposition to Christophe's rule had grown significantly in the northern provinces'; the insurgents hanged the new king on 18 October 1820; infobox 'Death of King Henry I: 8 October 1820'.

wars.name: War between Christophe's north and Pétion's south

zones.text: the border country between the two Haitian states; the pages name no place

wars.outcome: Stalemate: two states side by side until Christophe's death in 1820; Pétion died on 29 March 1818 and Boyer succeeded him.
wars.note: Pages disagree on the end: the Pétion page has a peace treaty in 1810 that 'split the country in two', the Kingdom page 'intermittently from 1807 until Pétion's death in 1818'.

certainty.note: The line between the north and Pétion's south is not described on any page opened; it is a de facto front, not a surveyed or treaty line.

sources.title: State of Haiti
sources.note: Founding 17 October 1806, Christophe president 17 February 1807, capital Milot, kingdom 28 March 1811.

sources.title: Kingdom of Haiti
sources.note: Proclamation 28 March 1811, coronation 2 June 1811, Cap-Henri, wars 1807-1818, 1820 revolt and death.

sources.title: Henri Christophe
sources.note: Elected president 17 February 1807, kingdom in the north, death 8 October 1820, Boyer's reunion.

sources.title: History of Haiti
sources.note: The 1806 split into north and south, 1811 kingdom, 1820 reunification; silent on borders.

sources.title: Alexandre Pétion
sources.note: Peace treaty of 1810 that split the country; Pétion's death 29 March 1818; Boyer's reunion.

notes:
Cliopatria lacks the Kingdom of Haiti; the am-08-a haiti dossier (slug haiti) records the split (October 1806) and the merge (1820) with counterpart kingdom-of-haiti, and this dossier mirrors them.
Border not settled: none of the five pages gives the north's departments or the line with the south (the Artibonite, Saint-Marc, the Goman rebellion at Grand'Anse and the 1810-1812 southern state are all absent from them); the four northern departments are the researcher's reading and the contest zone is confidence 1. A gap-filler should open the Spanish or French article on the 'Royaume d'Haïti' or 'Henri Christophe'.
Capitals: the State of Haiti page gives Milot, the Kingdom page Cap-Henri; Haiti's own dossier says Cap-Haïtien. Milot is not in the gazetteer (listed in the report) and its coordinates are approximate.
Dates: the Christophe page says the kingdom was created on 26 March 1811, the Kingdom and State pages 28 March 1811; 28 March is used.
